articles.title: Your first shift at the intake desk
articles.summary: Master the 5-step reception workflow: field registration, scanning vs syncing, physical verification, receipt confirmation, and downstream readiness.
articles.quick: Follow the 5-step intake workflow: locate expected samples, inspect physical material, record condition, assign Lab ID, and confirm receipt.
before: Confirm you are logged in with the appropriate laboratory role.
Verify the sample identifiers, assignment status and prerequisite steps.

steps.action: Open Reception (/reception). Use the barcode scanner or search filter to locate the expected sample pre-registered from KoBo.
steps.expected: The sample is displayed with status EXPECTED. Scanning finds a record and syncing imports data; neither alone constitutes physical receipt.

steps.action: Examine the physical container, label match, seal, soil moisture, and approximate weight. Record any damage, leakage, or insufficient quantity.
steps.expected: Non-conformances are documented. Severe non-conformance can be quarantined or rejected (RECEIVED_REJECTED) without entering analytical queues.

steps.action: Assign or verify the unique Laboratory ID (labId) and click Confirm Receipt.
steps.expected: Authoritative intake sets receptionDate to now() and transitions status to RECEIVED/ACCEPTED. Drying and preparation tasks unlock on technician workbenches (/workbench). Dashboard counters (Received Today) update strictly based on receptionDate.

fields: Verify container label matches system display.
articles.example: Synthetic example for Your first shift at the intake desk: follow the ordered controls with representative sample DEMO-001.
articles.success: The operation is recorded with a durable receipt, and the sample advances to the next workflow state.
articles.nextActor: Assigned colleague or laboratory manager

problems.symptom: An expected field sample is counted in Received Today or appears on technician workbenches before arrival.
problems.why: Sample status remains EXPECTED with receptionDate null. LIMS dashboard counters and analytical queues strictly require confirmed receptionDate.
problems.action: Locate the physical soil container, inspect its condition in Reception, and complete the Confirm Receipt action.

steps: Open Reception (/reception). Use the barcode scanner or search filter to locate the expected sample pre-registered from KoBo. (Expected: The sample is displayed with status EXPECTED. Scanning finds a record and syncing imports data; neither alone constitutes physical receipt.)

articles.title: Receive a project sample
articles.summary: Follow ID & Field, Condition, Analyses and Handover using a synthetic project sample.
articles.quick: Match the container label to the expected project sample record, record physical mass and condition exceptions, verify requested analyses, and complete receipt confirmation.
before: Have the physical material, label, delivery information and required intake measurements available.
Confirm your laboratory and project scope. Use the existing project record when one already represents the sample.
The exact final receipt control and any manager intake review depend on the deployed workflow; the writer must bind and verify those controls before publication.

steps.action: Open Reception and select the project. In ID & Field, find or scan the identifier on the physical label.
steps.expected: A matching source record is displayed. A KoBo submission is field provenance, not proof that the material arrived.

steps.action: Compare project, field identifier and displayed laboratory identifier. Check the source location and sampling information.
steps.expected: The correct project record is linked. If source coordinates exist but the draft is blank, preserve the discrepancy instead of inventing coordinates.

steps.action: Open Condition. Enter the actual received mass in the stated unit, the observed condition and the required compliance answers.
steps.expected: Missing values, insufficient mass or nonconformance are visible as specific issues rather than silently accepted defaults.

steps.action: Document any required exception reason. In Analyses, review the parameter names and method choices against the request.
steps.expected: The ordered work matches the request. Grouped analyses such as texture are handled according to the configured panel, not invented as unrelated tasks.

steps.action: Open Handover and review identity, condition, ordered analyses and outstanding issues. Use Save draft if the entry is not ready.
steps.expected: A saved draft remains distinct from an accepted receipt; it should not move unreceived material into drying workload.

steps.action: When complete, perform the verified final receipt action and inspect its confirmation and resulting intake state.
steps.expected: The application identifies what was received and whether another intake-review action remains. Final control binding is a required publication check for this exemplar.

steps.action: Check the sample label and the destination or handover details before transferring the physical material.
steps.expected: The next worker can identify the material and locate the corresponding tasks without duplicating intake.

problems.symptom: No location recorded after resuming

problems.symptom: Duplicate identifier
problems.why: More than one candidate or an existing receipt needs reconciliation.

steps: Open Reception and select the project. In ID & Field, find or scan the identifier on the physical label. (Expected: A matching source record is displayed. A KoBo submission is field provenance, not proof that the material arrived.)

Compare project, field identifier and displayed laboratory identifier. Check the source location and sampling information. (Expected: The correct project record is linked. If source coordinates exist but the draft is blank, preserve the discrepancy instead of inventing coordinates.)

Open Condition. Enter the actual received mass in the stated unit, the observed condition and the required compliance answers. (Expected: Missing values, insufficient mass or nonconformance are visible as specific issues rather than silently accepted defaults.)

Document any required exception reason. In Analyses, review the parameter names and method choices against the request. (Expected: The ordered work matches the request. Grouped analyses such as texture are handled according to the configured panel, not invented as unrelated tasks.)

Open Handover and review identity, condition, ordered analyses and outstanding issues. Use Save draft if the entry is not ready. (Expected: A saved draft remains distinct from an accepted receipt; it should not move unreceived material into drying workload.)

When complete, perform the verified final receipt action and inspect its confirmation and resulting intake state. (Expected: The application identifies what was received and whether another intake-review action remains. Final control binding is a required publication check for this exemplar.)

Check the sample label and the destination or handover details before transferring the physical material. (Expected: The next worker can identify the material and locate the corresponding tasks without duplicating intake.)
articles.caution: Avoid: No location recorded after resuming

articles.title: Confirm sample drying and find its receipt
articles.summary: Finish the required checks, confirm completion and verify the confirmation receipt.
articles.quick: Complete the required physical checks, select Confirm Complete, and verify the confirmation receipt. A checked box alone is not evidence that the server accepted completion.
before: Match the physical label to the laboratory and field identifiers shown for the task.
Use the drying procedure assigned by the laboratory. This guide does not prescribe a temperature, duration or endpoint.
Use a working connection for this confirmation workflow. Do not assume that checking items on screen has queued an offline confirmation.
If Legacy Completion — Evidence Gap is displayed, use the evidence-gap procedure; a new tick cannot establish missing historical evidence.

sections.title: 1. Check the sample and perform the work

steps.action: In Workbench, open the assigned Sample drying task. Compare its sample identifier with the container and bench log.
steps.expected: You are documenting the physical material actually handled, under the correct task and laboratory.

steps.action: Read every displayed checklist item. Perform and verify the drying work under the applicable lab procedure; record its required evidence in the designated records.
steps.expected: The checklist reflects work that has happened. A tutorial, task assignment or sample receipt is not evidence that drying is complete.

steps.action: Select each checklist item only after checking it. Confirm that the row shows Operational checklist complete.
steps.expected: All required checks are marked. The final confirmation action becomes available; the checks alone are not yet the durable receipt.

steps.action: Select Confirm Complete on that row. For a permitted bulk action, compare every selected sample first and use the displayed Confirm … Complete count.
steps.expected: The operation is sent for confirmation. Do not select unperformed samples merely because they share a batch.

steps.action: Look for Checklist Verified and read the receipt identifier, recorded user and time. Keep the receipt reference if another page seems inconsistent.
steps.expected: The saved receipt replaces the editable checklist. The application has evidence for this operational confirmation.

steps.action: Return to the relevant work queue and inspect the next task's readiness.
steps.expected: A drying requirement can be satisfied while preparation, assignment or instrument requirements still block an analysis. Drying does not automatically complete those separate requirements.

fields: Confirm the actions actually performed under the assigned procedure.
Evidence returned for the confirmation, not a number to invent.
Read the remaining blocker and responsible role.
articles.example: Synthetic example for Confirm sample drying and find its receipt: follow the ordered controls with representative sample DEMO-001.
articles.success: The drying task shows a green verified badge with timestamp, receipt ID and operator identity. Downstream preparation tasks unlock.
articles.nextActor: Preparation technician or analytical analyst

problems.symptom: All checks are ticked but no receipt appears
problems.why: The checklist may not have been confirmed, or the request did not complete.
problems.action: Inspect the confirmation state and connection. Check for an existing receipt before retrying; do not repeat the physical work only to change the screen.

problems.symptom: Sample page still looks incomplete
problems.why: The page may show a different task, attempt or aggregate sample state, or a display defect.
problems.action: Compare task/attempt and receipt. Preserve the reference and report the contradiction if it persists. Do not use a second completion control as a workaround.

problems.symptom: The analysis is still blocked
problems.why: Another prerequisite remains unmet.
problems.action: Open the specific blocker explanation. Finish only the work assigned and permitted to you.

articles.title: Confirm preparation for the assigned method
articles.summary: Check the applicable preparation steps and record completion for the correct material.
articles.quick: Check the applicable preparation steps and record completion for the correct material. In /workbench, verify the physical soil material, record actual air-drying temperature (< 40 °C), duration, and sieve mesh size (e.g., 2 mm or < 100 µm for MIR), and click Confirm Complete to unlock downstream bench analyses.
before: Confirm the sample has completed Reception (REGISTERED) and physically matches the barcode on the drying tray or sieve.
Check whether your laboratory policy requires second-person gate verification (gate.verificationRequired).

steps.action: Open /workbench and select the sample or batch of samples in the DRYING or PREPARATION queue.
steps.expected: The pre-analytical checklist displays the required drying (< 40 °C) and sieving/grinding parameters.

steps.action: Complete the physical checks, record actual oven/room temperature, duration, sieve size, and final prepared mass (Check the applicable preparation steps and record completion for the correct material.).
steps.expected: Each selected sample shows validated preparation parameters; any sample not physically prepared must be deselected before bulk confirmation.

steps.action: Click Confirm Complete (and obtain supervisor verification if gate.verificationRequired is enabled) and inspect the confirmation receipt.
steps.expected: A permanent PreparationRecord receipt is saved, and dependent wet-chemistry and spectroscopy work items transition from blocked to READY_FOR_ANALYSIS.

fields: Keep < 40 °C for routine air-dry chemistry so volatile N and organic matter are preserved.

sections.title: 2. Compare the records and resolve the blocker

steps.action: With a receipt present, compare the sample identifier and preparation task/attempt with the sample page entry.

steps.action: Read the exact readiness explanation for the analysis you want to perform next.
steps.expected: It identifies the unresolved prerequisite or capability. Another required preparation or instrument condition can remain after one task is complete.

steps.action: If the same task and attempt still contradict the receipt, send the manager or application support the page names, time, task and receipt references through the configured channel.
steps.expected: The discrepancy can be reproduced and corrected without losing the original operational evidence.

before: Use your own account and confirm the laboratory shown in the application.
Have the instrument output or bench record, the sample identifiers and the required method metadata available.
Confirm that the tasks are assigned to you and their preparation and equipment requirements are satisfied. A different pH method or measurement basis belongs in a different method group.
For this example, use the connected workflow. Check the separate offline guide for actions actually supported by your downloaded work pack.

sections.title: 1. Select the work and prepare the data

steps.action: Open Workbench and choose the required analysis method in Worksheet. Compare the displayed parameter and method with your bench record.
steps.expected: The worksheet contains the assigned tasks for that method. The same sample may legitimately have other analyses elsewhere.

steps.action: For a spreadsheet paste, prepare two columns: Sample ID and Result Value. Copy the data rows, without column headings. Keep identifiers as text so leading zeros are not lost.
steps.expected: Each result remains attached to its own identifier. Do not rely on the worksheet and spreadsheet having the same row order.

steps.action: Select Paste Values, paste the two columns and select Preview Matches & Exclusions.
steps.expected: A preview identifies matched rows and explains duplicates, unassigned samples, sealed tasks, invalid numbers and prerequisite failures.

steps.action: Compare the included identifiers and values with the source record. Resolve errors at their cause. If 38 of 40 rows match, do not describe the import as 40 completed results.
steps.expected: You can account for every source row as included or excluded. A sample with an unresolved prerequisite remains blocked.

steps.action: Select Apply 38 Matched Drafts, or the actual displayed count. Check the worksheet values and required instrument, units or basis metadata.
steps.expected: Values appear as drafts. Applying them has not yet recorded the determinations or sent them to the manager.

steps.action: Select the intended worksheet rows and choose Review Completion. Inspect Included Determinations and Excluded / Incomplete.
steps.expected: The application explains which individual determinations can be recorded. An excluded item stays outside the operation.

steps.action: Read the confirmation, select it only after checking the entries, and choose Record N Determinations.
steps.expected: The eligible results are recorded. This is still a separate event from reviewer submission; preserve the confirmation if the response is uncertain.

sections.title: 4. Send the correct samples for review

steps.action: Open Ready to Submit. Inspect each selected sample's included analyses and whether the submission is FULL or PARTIAL.
steps.expected: A partial submission contains the completed determinations shown; it does not mean all requested analyses are finished.

steps.action: Add useful reviewer notes if needed, read the confirmation, and select Submit N Samples for Review.
steps.expected: The server confirms the submission. Submitted work is no longer ordinary editable draft work.

steps.action: Open Sent & Completed and verify the submitted work or receipt. If the manager cannot find it, provide that receipt and check the laboratory and queue filters before repeating anything.
steps.expected: The manager can inspect the submitted version in the review queue. Approval and report release are later decisions.

fields: Use an identifier recognized for an assigned task in this method group.
Use the observed value and the configured unit/basis. Blank and zero have different meanings.
Match the configured variant to the bench record; do not merge different extraction bases.
articles.success: The submitted determinations show Sent & Completed, the sample status advances to SUBMITTED, and the manager queue reflects the new submission.
articles.nextActor: Laboratory manager or authorized reviewer

problems.why: Preview validation found specific row problems.
problems.action: Use each exclusion reason. Apply only the intended valid rows, and retain a list of unresolved rows for correction.

problems.why: A draft or recorded result has not necessarily been submitted.
problems.action: Check Ready to Submit and the actual submission receipt. Do not re-enter the same measurements on the sample page.

before: Confirm the method variant matches your bench SOP (for example, pH 1:2.5 H2O vs. 0.01M CaCl2, or Olsen P vs. Bray-1 P).

steps.action: Open /workbench and select the specific analytical method, multi-fraction panel (Sand/Silt/Clay), or spectral modality (MIR 4000-400 cm-1 / Vis-NIR 350-2500 nm).
steps.expected: The method-specific input schema, canonical unit, and QC evaluation rules (QcRule) load.

steps.action: Enter raw measurements or upload spectral files, ensuring all panel components and batch QC positions (BLANK, DUPLICATE, LRM, CRM, CCV) are recorded (Explain the configured pH variant, result entry and QC links without prescribing a new SOP.).
steps.expected: The LIMS calculates concentrations, checks texture closure (Sand + Silt + Clay = 100% ± crossCheck.textureClosureTolerancePct), and evaluates QC pass/warn/fail.

steps.action: Inspect any QC warnings, replicate repeatability r checks, or spectral quality flags, and submit only validated runs (or trigger a Repeat / Bracketed Repeat if a control failed).
steps.expected: Measured reference results and spectral predictions remain clearly distinguished by provenance (MEASURED vs. DERIVED vs. PREDICTED).

fields: One standardized unit per analysis (e.g., g/kg, mg/kg, cmol(+)/kg) and AIR_DRY / OVEN_DRY basis
Do not mix units or extraction bases in the same batch; legacy synonyms normalize automatically.
Enter all three particle-size fractions together as one panel so USDA Texture Class derives accurately.
Evaluated against your lab policy and method QcRule; never ignore a failed control in REQUIRED_BLOCKING mode.
articles.example: Enter Sand = 45.0%, Silt = 35.0%, Clay = 20.0% (Sum = 100.0%, Loam) with passing LRM recovery (98%), then record and submit the panel.
articles.success: Method measurements, panel closure checks, spectral QC validations, and batch control evaluations are complete and ready for technical review.

articles.title: Import MIR or NIR spectra for assigned work
articles.summary: Follow Identify & Upload, Match & Inspect, Confirm Import and Receipt.
articles.quick: Upload instrument export files, match each acquisition to the assigned sample and replicate number, inspect wavenumber and QC checks, and confirm the import receipt.
before: Have the original instrument export, instrument identity and sample/scan identifiers available.
Use an export/profile actually supported and verified for your instrument and method. A file extension in a picker is not proof that every vendor variant is supported.
Use the lab's approved acquisition and spectral QC procedure. This article does not define scan settings or acceptance thresholds.

steps.action: Open spectral import from the assigned Workbench method. In Identify & Upload, select the verified spectrometer and provide required run/acquisition details.
steps.expected: The import is associated with the correct instrument and method context. Missing or ineligible instruments need correction, not a free-text substitute.

steps.action: Select the original export files and continue to staging preview.
steps.expected: The system reports recognized files and parsing problems. A staged file has not yet completed the task or been accepted for reporting.

steps.action: In Match & Inspect, compare each detected sample/scan identifier with the label and assigned task.
steps.expected: Each included spectrum has an intentional sample/task match. Similar filenames and row order alone do not establish identity.

steps.action: Inspect the plot, axis type and unit, acquisition metadata, replicates and reported validation issues.
steps.expected: You can recognize an unexpected axis, missing range or wrong sample match and follow the applicable profile/QC requirements.

steps.action: Resolve or exclude failed and unmatched entries with the available workflow, preserving the original files and exclusion reasons.
steps.expected: The import count reflects only the intended included items; excluded files remain accounted for.

steps.action: Review the final mapping in Confirm Import, make the required confirmation and complete the import.
steps.expected: The Receipt step shows which items were imported and which were not. Use the actual receipt before retrying an uncertain upload.

steps.action: Open the linked spectrum in Spectral Library and inspect its sample association and review/QC state.
steps.expected: The original spectrum can be traced. Imported, quality-accepted, predicted and report-approved are not interchangeable states.

steps.action: If a prediction is produced, inspect its model/version and applicability separately from reference measurements and the final result review.
steps.expected: A model output is not silently represented as a measured wet-chemistry result or an approved report.

fields: Original supported instrument export, with acquisition provenance.
A synthetic fixture supplied for the configured import profile
Read the declared units and representation from the profile/export.

Sample and assigned task linked to the scan.

articles.title: Review an intake and its exceptions
articles.summary: Check received evidence, analysis scope and unresolved nonconformance.
articles.quick: Check received evidence, analysis scope and unresolved nonconformance. Use /manager-queue to perform Stage 1 (Method/Batch technical review) and Stage 2 (Whole-sample holistic approval), verify the saved Reported Value Selection and soil chemistry cross-checks, issue official PDF Certificates of Analysis, or manage post-report Amendments and Revisions (Rev 2+).
before: Remember that when review.secondPersonRequired is enabled, you cannot approve a batch or sample for which you recorded the bench results yourself.
Verify that all batch QC controls (Blanks, Duplicates, LRMs, CRMs) and pre-analytical gates are resolved before final approval.

steps.action: Open /manager-queue and inspect the submitted batch (Stage 1) or whole sample across all requested parameters (Stage 2).
steps.expected: You see all analytical attempts (R1, R2), replicate agreement, QC evaluations, and cross-parameter plausibility checks (CEC vs. Sum of Bases, Texture Closure, C:N ratio, pH vs. CaCO3).

steps.action: Verify the Reported Value Selection (MEAN_IF_WITHIN_R, LATEST_VALID, or REVIEWER_PICKS) and choose the appropriate review action (Check received evidence, analysis scope and unresolved nonconformance.).
steps.expected: Approved work locks the saved ReportedValueSelection; returned work creates a new repeat attempt (R2/R3) with your written instructions while keeping R1 sealed.

steps.action: For approved samples, issue the PDF Certificate of Analysis (RPT-...). If a correction is ever needed after a report is issued, click Amend Sample (CLERICAL or SCIENTIFIC) and issue an Amended Report Revision (Rev 2+).
steps.expected: Opening a scientific amendment immediately marks Rev 1 WITHDRAWN on public QR links; issuing Rev 2 marks Rev 1 SUPERSEDED and prints the ISO 17025 replacement banner with †/‡ change markers.

fields: Used by PDF reports, CSV/Excel exports, and v1 Data Exchange; never edit a released result in place.
Reviewer disposition on an individual work item
Returning creates a new bench attempt (R2) with a mandatory reason; waiving/excluding requires manager justification.
Scientific amendments require second-person approval when report.amendmentRequiresSecondPerson is enabled and immediately withdraw the old PDF.
articles.example: In /manager-queue, verify sample NRL-26-000142C has passing QC and no cross-check warnings, click Approve Sample, and issue Certificate RPT-NRL-2026-00042 (Rev 1).
articles.success: The review decision, saved Reported Value, or report revision is permanently logged with electronic approver attribution.
articles.nextActor: Lab Technician (if returned for repeat) or Client / Project Manager (when report is issued)

steps.action: If acceptable, perform the authorized review action and verify its confirmation and resulting state.
steps.expected: The application records the reviewer decision. It does not automatically establish that a final report was generated or delivered.

steps.expected: Unsubmitted analyses, unresolved QC, nonconformance or incomplete evidence remain visible; freshly received material cannot be treated as fully analyzed.

problems.symptom: The technician says results were saved, but Review Submissions is empty

steps.action: When reconnected (or before switching user accounts on a shared tablet), synchronize the queue and resolve any server revision conflicts without clearing browser storage prematurely.
steps.expected: Synced items receive a server timestamp receipt, and switching accounts safely isolates laboratory data.

fields: Device Draft vs. Queued vs. Synced
Managers cannot see offline work until synchronization completes and returns a server receipt.

Signing out or changing lab scope

sections.title: 1. Reconnect without losing the local record

steps.action: Restore a stable connection and confirm the signed-in account and laboratory.
steps.expected: The queued work is reconciled under the correct identity; another lab's cache is not used.

steps.action: Open the actual synchronization status or pending-work view supplied by the application.
steps.expected: You can distinguish queued actions from completed server operations and see the recorded failure reasons.

steps.action: Inspect each completed action and its server confirmation. For a partial sync, compare the number and identities of completed and still-pending actions.
steps.expected: A global online indicator is not mistaken for successful submission of every result or attachment.

steps.action: For a retryable transport failure, use the application's retry/reconciliation action after checking whether the server already recorded it.
steps.expected: The original operation identity is preserved; an uncertain response does not produce a duplicate result.

steps.action: For a conflict, compare the local entry and current server state and follow the permitted resolution. If work was reassigned or approved, involve the responsible manager.
steps.expected: The application does not silently overwrite another person's work or an approved result.

steps.action: After successful synchronization, inspect the relevant Workbench or intake receipt and resulting task state.
steps.expected: A synchronized draft may still require recording or reviewer submission. Sync success and analytical approval remain separate.

articles.title: Configure a laboratory and its scope
articles.summary: Explain lab identity, configuration ownership and changes affecting users.
articles.quick: Explain lab identity, configuration ownership and changes affecting users. In /admin/labs, configure your laboratory's policy preset (ISO17025_STRICT, BASIC, or ADVISORY) and custom overrides, manage user roles and lab scopes, maintain the analysis catalogue and method QcRules, and manage scoped Data Exchange API keys.
before: Confirm you are signed in as a Lab Manager (for single-lab settings) or Super Admin (for global multi-lab settings and API keys).
Prepare a clear written reason whenever saving changes to Laboratory Policy or Method QC Rules.

steps.action: Open /admin/labs and verify the target laboratory or system configuration tab.
steps.expected: Current settings, active preset badges (ISO17025_STRICT, BASIC, ADVISORY), user role assignments, or method definitions load.

steps.action: Configure the setting, user role, analysis/method contract, branding, or legacy import mapping (Explain lab identity, configuration ownership and changes affecting users.).
steps.expected: The LIMS validates compatibility (such as checking for POLICY_QC_RULE_CONFLICT and ensuring one canonical unit per analysis) without mutating historical approved results or issued reports.

steps.action: Save the configuration with an audit reason and verify the change in the Audit Log or preview.
steps.expected: New batches and intakes immediately use the updated configuration, while historical evaluations retain their original policy snapshot.

fields: 1. Method QcRule → 2. Analysis Override → 3. Lab Setting → 4. Preset
Nothing is hard-coded to one lab; customize frequencies, batch sizes, and review rules per lab and method.
User role (RECEPTION, TECHNICIAN, REVIEWER, LAB_MANAGER, SUPER_ADMIN) + labId
Every operational user and external API key must have an explicit laboratory scope (fail-closed).
Rotate slims_live_... keys without downtime; never paste plaintext API secrets into support tickets.
articles.example: In Settings → Laboratory Policy, select ISO17025_STRICT, adjust duplicateEvery to 10 with reason "2026 Quality Manual rev 4", and click Save Policy Changes.
articles.success: The administrative configuration is validated, saved with a versioned audit record, and active for new laboratory operations.
articles.nextActor: Laboratory Manager, Staff Users, or External NSIS Administrator

articles.title: Confirm sample drying and find its receipt (bench-drying)
articles.summary: Finish the required checks, confirm completion and verify the confirmation receipt. [Canonical successor: prep-drying]
articles.quick: Complete the required physical checks, select Confirm Complete, and verify the confirmation receipt. A checked box alone is not evidence that the server accepted completion.
before: Match the physical label to the laboratory and field identifiers shown for the task.
Use the drying procedure assigned by the laboratory. This guide does not prescribe a temperature, duration or endpoint.
Use a working connection for this confirmation workflow. Do not assume that checking items on screen has queued an offline confirmation.
If Legacy Completion — Evidence Gap is displayed, use the evidence-gap procedure; a new tick cannot establish missing historical evidence.

sections.title: 1. Check the sample and perform the work

steps.action: In Workbench, open the assigned Sample drying task. Compare its sample identifier with the container and bench log.
steps.expected: You are documenting the physical material actually handled, under the correct task and laboratory.

steps.action: Read every displayed checklist item. Perform and verify the drying work under the applicable lab procedure; record its required evidence in the designated records.
steps.expected: The checklist reflects work that has happened. A tutorial, task assignment or sample receipt is not evidence that drying is complete.

steps.action: Select each checklist item only after checking it. Confirm that the row shows Operational checklist complete.
steps.expected: All required checks are marked. The final confirmation action becomes available; the checks alone are not yet the durable receipt.

steps.action: Select Confirm Complete on that row. For a permitted bulk action, compare every selected sample first and use the displayed Confirm … Complete count.
steps.expected: The operation is sent for confirmation. Do not select unperformed samples merely because they share a batch.

steps.action: Look for Checklist Verified and read the receipt identifier, recorded user and time. Keep the receipt reference if another page seems inconsistent.
steps.expected: The saved receipt replaces the editable checklist. The application has evidence for this operational confirmation.

steps.action: Return to the relevant work queue and inspect the next task's readiness.
steps.expected: A drying requirement can be satisfied while preparation, assignment or instrument requirements still block an analysis. Drying does not automatically complete those separate requirements.

fields: Confirm the actions actually performed under the assigned procedure.
Evidence returned for the confirmation, not a number to invent.
Read the remaining blocker and responsible role.
articles.example: Synthetic example for Confirm sample drying and find its receipt: follow the ordered controls with representative sample DEMO-001.
articles.success: The drying task shows a green verified badge with timestamp, receipt ID and operator identity. Downstream preparation tasks unlock.

problems.why: The page may show a different task, attempt or aggregate sample state, or a display defect.
problems.action: Compare task/attempt and receipt. Preserve the reference and report the contradiction if it persists. Do not use a second completion control as a workaround.

problems.symptom: The analysis is still blocked
problems.why: Another prerequisite remains unmet.
problems.action: Open the specific blocker explanation. Finish only the work assigned and permitted to you.

before: Use your own account and confirm the laboratory shown in the application.

sections.title: 1. Select the work and prepare the data

steps.action: Open Workbench and choose the required analysis method in Worksheet. Compare the displayed parameter and method with your bench record.
steps.expected: The worksheet contains the assigned tasks for that method. The same sample may legitimately have other analyses elsewhere.

steps.action: For a spreadsheet paste, prepare two columns: Sample ID and Result Value. Copy the data rows, without column headings. Keep identifiers as text so leading zeros are not lost.
steps.expected: Each result remains attached to its own identifier. Do not rely on the worksheet and spreadsheet having the same row order.

articles.title: Inspect and compare spectra in the library (connect-library)
articles.summary: Explain axes, acquisition metadata, replicates, QC and original files. [Canonical successor: method-spectral-inspect]
articles.quick: Explain axes, acquisition metadata, replicates, QC and original files. [Canonical successor: method-spectral-inspect] Select the exact method SOP variant on the Workbench or Spectral Library (/spectral-library), verify the canonical unit, moisture basis, and batch QC controls (Blank, Duplicate, LRM/CRM, ICV/CCV), and review derived or spectral quality flags before submitting.
before: Confirm the method variant matches your bench SOP (for example, pH 1:2.5 H2O vs. 0.01M CaCl2, or Olsen P vs. Bray-1 P).
Verify that required batch QC samples and active Reference Material lots are included in the run.

steps.action: Open /spectral-library and select the specific analytical method, multi-fraction panel (Sand/Silt/Clay), or spectral modality (MIR 4000-400 cm-1 / Vis-NIR 350-2500 nm).
steps.expected: The method-specific input schema, canonical unit, and QC evaluation rules (QcRule) load.

steps.action: Enter raw measurements or upload spectral files, ensuring all panel components and batch QC positions (BLANK, DUPLICATE, LRM, CRM, CCV) are recorded (Explain axes, acquisition metadata, replicates, QC and original files. [Canonical successor: method-spectral-inspect]).
steps.expected: The LIMS calculates concentrations, checks texture closure (Sand + Silt + Clay = 100% ± crossCheck.textureClosureTolerancePct), and evaluates QC pass/warn/fail.

steps.action: Inspect any QC warnings, replicate repeatability r checks, or spectral quality flags, and submit only validated runs (or trigger a Repeat / Bracketed Repeat if a control failed).
steps.expected: Measured reference results and spectral predictions remain clearly distinguished by provenance (MEASURED vs. DERIVED vs. PREDICTED).

fields: One standardized unit per analysis (e.g., g/kg, mg/kg, cmol(+)/kg) and AIR_DRY / OVEN_DRY basis
Do not mix units or extraction bases in the same batch; legacy synonyms normalize automatically.
Enter all three particle-size fractions together as one panel so USDA Texture Class derives accurately.
Evaluated against your lab policy and method QcRule; never ignore a failed control in REQUIRED_BLOCKING mode.
articles.example: Enter Sand = 45.0%, Silt = 35.0%, Clay = 20.0% (Sum = 100.0%, Loam) with passing LRM recovery (98%), then record and submit the panel.
articles.success: Method measurements, panel closure checks, spectral QC validations, and batch control evaluations are complete and ready for technical review.
articles.nextActor: Technical Reviewer or Laboratory Manager

problems.symptom: A successful upload is mistaken for accepted spectral quality.
problems.why: Different method variants or unit scales were mixed in one batch, Sand + Silt + Clay did not sum to 100% ± tolerance, or a batch QC control failed.
problems.action: Verify the method SOP and canonical unit, check all three texture fractions on the hydrometer/pipette worksheet, and re-run or disposition any failed QC batch before reporting.

articles.title: Configure an analysis without breaking existing work (manage-catalogue)
articles.summary: Trace selection, input schema, prerequisites, methods and reports. [Canonical successor: admin-catalogue]
articles.quick: Trace selection, input schema, prerequisites, methods and reports. [Canonical successor: admin-catalogue] In /admin?tab=lab-config, configure your laboratory's policy preset (ISO17025_STRICT, BASIC, or ADVISORY) and custom overrides, manage user roles and lab scopes, maintain the analysis catalogue and method QcRules, and manage scoped Data Exchange API keys.
before: Confirm you are signed in as a Lab Manager (for single-lab settings) or Super Admin (for global multi-lab settings and API keys).
Prepare a clear written reason whenever saving changes to Laboratory Policy or Method QC Rules.

steps.action: Open /admin?tab=lab-config and verify the target laboratory or system configuration tab.
steps.expected: Current settings, active preset badges (ISO17025_STRICT, BASIC, ADVISORY), user role assignments, or method definitions load.

steps.action: Configure the setting, user role, analysis/method contract, branding, or legacy import mapping (Trace selection, input schema, prerequisites, methods and reports. [Canonical successor: admin-catalogue]).
steps.expected: The LIMS validates compatibility (such as checking for POLICY_QC_RULE_CONFLICT and ensuring one canonical unit per analysis) without mutating historical approved results or issued reports.

steps.action: Save the configuration with an audit reason and verify the change in the Audit Log or preview.
steps.expected: New batches and intakes immediately use the updated configuration, while historical evaluations retain their original policy snapshot.

fields: 1. Method QcRule → 2. Analysis Override → 3. Lab Setting → 4. Preset
Nothing is hard-coded to one lab; customize frequencies, batch sizes, and review rules per lab and method.
User role (RECEPTION, TECHNICIAN, REVIEWER, LAB_MANAGER, SUPER_ADMIN) + labId
Every operational user and external API key must have an explicit laboratory scope (fail-closed).
Rotate slims_live_... keys without downtime; never paste plaintext API secrets into support tickets.
articles.example: In Settings → Laboratory Policy, select ISO17025_STRICT, adjust duplicateEvery to 10 with reason "2026 Quality Manual rev 4", and click Save Policy Changes.
articles.success: The administrative configuration is validated, saved with a versioned audit record, and active for new laboratory operations.
articles.nextActor: Laboratory Manager, Staff Users, or External NSIS Administrator

problems.symptom: A code-only catalogue entry creates an unusable worksheet.
problems.why: Your account lacks Lab Manager / Super Admin authority for the target lab, a new policy conflicts with an incomplete method QcRule, or an API key has an empty lab scope.
problems.action: Check your role and selected laboratory scope, resolve any highlighted validation warning on the form, and verify the saved entry in /admin/audit.

before: Confirm your active laboratory badge and role in the top header before working in /profile.
Check whether any filters (Project, Status, or Assigned To) are narrowing the current list.

steps.action: Open /profile and inspect the queue counters, status badges, and active laboratory filter.
steps.expected: You see only records scoped to your authorized laboratory and projects.

steps.action: Perform the workflow check: Apply session or profile settings without changing laboratory data. [Canonical successor: start-settings]
steps.expected: Each item clearly shows its current lifecycle status (EXPECTED, REGISTERED, IN_PREP, READY_FOR_ANALYSIS, SUBMITTED, REVIEWED, APPROVED, or REPORTED) and next owner.

steps.action: Open an individual record or receipt to verify who recorded the previous step before taking or handing off the next action.
steps.expected: Audit history and prerequisite receipts remain intact without accidental edits.

fields: Active facility filter in the header
Confirm it matches your physical laboratory before acting.
Current stage of the sample or work item
Distinguish EXPECTED/SAVED drafts from SUBMITTED or APPROVED records.
Role responsible for the next step
Hand off to Reception, Technician, Reviewer, or Lab Manager as shown.
articles.example: In /profile, check sample NRL-26-000142C: verify its status badge and prerequisite receipts before starting or reviewing work.
articles.success: You have verified the current queue state, ownership, and evidence in your laboratory scope without altering locked records.
articles.nextActor: Assigned Lab Technician, Reviewer, or Lab Manager

problems.why: A queue filter is hiding records, the item is still in an earlier prerequisite stage (such as EXPECTED or IN_PREP), or your role is read-only for this step.
problems.action: Reset queue filters in /profile, inspect the sample's workflow stage and prerequisite receipts, and confirm role permissions with your Lab Manager.

articles.title: Recover from a blank page or failed application update (manage-load-error)
articles.summary: Protect drafts and use verified retry/update behavior before escalating. [Canonical successor: quality-loading]
articles.quick: Protect drafts and use verified retry/update behavior before escalating. [Canonical successor: quality-loading] Use /help to inspect the full before/after Audit Log, evaluate batch QC alerts and Shewhart control charts, open and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCR / CAPA), trace repeat attempts (R1, R2) and Report Revisions (Rev 1, Rev 2), or safely recover from browser/update errors.
before: Identify the exact Laboratory Sample Code, Batch ID, Report Number (RPT-...), or timestamp involved.
If recovering from a loading error on a bench device, do not clear browser storage before checking for unsynchronized offline drafts.

steps.action: Open /help and filter by sample code, batch ID, actor, date range, or alert status.
steps.expected: The complete chronological evidence trail loads—including raw attempts, QC evaluations, policy snapshots, and report revisions.

steps.action: Inspect the quality evidence or execute the recovery step (Protect drafts and use verified retry/update behavior before escalating. [Canonical successor: quality-loading]).
steps.expected: You can distinguish an automated file-upload check from analytical batch QC (BLANK, DUPLICATE, LRM, CRM, ICV/CCV), and trace every repeat (R1 → R2) or amended report (WITHDRAWN / SUPERSEDED → Rev 2).

steps.action: Record the required QC disposition, Non-Conformance Report (NCR) root cause and corrective action, or support ticket with minimal non-sensitive evidence.
steps.expected: Quality decisions and CAPA actions are permanently linked to the affected batch or sample without silently overwriting historical data.

fields: Analytical Batch QC vs. Import Check
File parsing success only means the file was readable; batch approval requires passing analytical QC or a Manager caveat disposition.
Required when attempts exceed repeats.maxAttemptsBeforeNcr or on major deviations
Documents description, root cause, containment, and corrective action (CAPA) before closure.
Public QR links immediately stop serving WITHDRAWN/SUPERSEDED PDFs and display a plain-text notice.
articles.example: In /qa, open failed batch BATCH-2026-0414, log NCR-2026-009 ("Olsen P reagent contamination in Blank"), trigger Repeat Batch (R2), and verify closure.
articles.success: Quality evidence, audit lineage, NCR corrective actions, or application recovery steps are completed with full traceability.
articles.nextActor: Quality Manager, Laboratory Manager, or Technical Support

problems.symptom: Repeated refresh or storage clearing loses unsynchronized work.
problems.why: An analytical QC failure or repeat threshold (maxAttemptsBeforeNcr) requires a documented disposition/NCR, an outdated public report link was used after an amendment, or local browser cache held a stale bundle.
problems.action: Follow the linked Batch ID or Sample ID in /qa and /admin/audit, verify the latest Report Revision in /result-reports, and preserve unsynced drafts before reloading the app.
